ctaLinks.copyText: Replace ad-hoc prompts with a defensible SPIKE.
ctaLinks.subtitle: Turn a vague feature ask into a PRD with acceptance criteria, risks, and rejection rationale before any agent runs.

stages.description: What an ungoverned agentic workflow actually looks like: a vague Slack prompt, a confident but wrong agent run, no traceable artifacts, and no memory carried forward. The cost is hidden in re-work, not visible in the token bill.

steps.description: A one-line Slack message kicks off the work. No spec attached.
steps.label: Vague ask lands

prd.content:
<!-- No PRD exists. The agent will infer requirements from
     the Slack thread and recent chat context. -->

Inferred from Slack:

> "ship the new onboarding flow this week"

Open questions (never written down):
  - Which onboarding flow? (B2B? Consumer?)
  - What does "ship" mean? (Beta? GA?)
  - Who is the owner if it breaks in prod?
prd.title: PRD (none)

terminal: $ slack #builds "hey can we ship the new onboarding flow this week"
> No PRD, no acceptance criteria, no owner.

steps.description: Engineer pastes the Slack thread into an agent. No system prompt, no role, no plan.
steps.label: Agent spun up

agents.content:
generic-agent (unscoped)
  Inferred to be: PM + architect + frontend + reviewer.
  No separation of concerns. No reviewer agent.
  Failure mode: one model carries all responsibility;
  no second opinion before output ships.
agents.title: Agent roles (implicit)

terminal: No system prompt. No role. No tools enumerated.

steps.description: Agent emits a 'plan' that contradicts unstated constraints. No one notices.
steps.label: Confident wrong plan

plan.content:
## Onboarding flow rewrite — plan (draft, agent)

| Phase | Task                              | Est  |
|-------|-----------------------------------|------|
| 1     | Replace Auth0 with Clerk          | 2 d  |
| 2     | Drop legacy mobile webview support | 1 d  |
| 3     | Ship behind feature flag           | 0.5 d|

**Assumptions made silently:**
- "New flow" means new auth provider. (Wrong; PM meant copy + visual refresh.)
- Legacy mobile is deprecated. (Wrong; 31% of users.)
- There is a feature flag service. (No.)
plan.title: Agent-generated plan (contradicts unstated constraints)

steps.description: Engineer accepts the plan and starts work. No PRD comparison, no PM sign-off.
steps.label: No verification

progress.content:
# No progress file exists. Status is in the engineer's head
# and the agent has no persistent memory.
status: unknown
blockers: []
assumptions_validated: []
owner: implicit
notes: |
  We have no record of which tasks were done, which were
  abandoned, or which were silently re-scoped mid-flight.
progress.title: Progress tracking (none)

terminal: > 'looks fine, I'll figure out the mobile thing later'

steps.description: Staging breaks on mobile. The agent's assumptions weren't validated against reality.
steps.label: Reality bites

progress.content:
status: in-progress (regressed)
completed_tasks: 2
regressed_tasks: 1
blockers:
  - legacy mobile webview support was not deprecated
  - feature flag service does not exist
  - PM intent was 'visual refresh', not 'auth rewrite'
rework_estimate_days: 2
rework_token_estimate: 220000
progress.title: Progress (reconstructed post-hoc)

terminal: 812df3a  drop legacy webview shim  <-- the regression

steps.description: Agent has no session memory. Engineer re-pastes context. Token bill compounds.
steps.label: Re-prompt from scratch

agents.content:
generic-agent (unscoped, again)
  Still no role separation. The same model that proposed
  the wrong plan is now correcting it without a reviewer.
  No spike-writer. No planner. No progress agent.
agents.title: Agent role (still unscoped)

terminal: No memory of previous session. No diff awareness.

steps.description: No PRD, no plan, no progress file. The next session starts from zero.
steps.label: Session ends, memory dies
